item: Operator-adapted opposing edge tests with exceptional discard sets, plus incidence averaging (paper I32+I33, using the records lemma I30/I31), for Lipschitz-free spaces over uniformly discrete blocks
item_type: F3 (lemma-level device inside a witness construction)
analyst_note: Text-level work only. The Lean was not compiled (no local toolchain). Web tools hit their session quota; outside references come from a subagent that used the arXiv API/full texts where marked [subagent-verified]. Others are marked [unverified].
lean_status_why: `MetricBlock.edge_test` (ScalarTests.lean:119) is the paper's Lemma edge-test almost verbatim: a 1-Lipschitz f into [−L,L] equal to b_x off E_e and −b_y off E_ē, built by McShane extension and clipping from the record/exceptional-direction lemma. The averaging is `signed_incidence_obstruction` (SignedTests.lean:207), with the paper's constants (3L/2, 2L, 1/(20V), L = 10p). It sits on the comparator path of both DiscreteLipschitzFree and RealL1Renorming. Only the graph supply around the item takes a different route (deterministic, below).

lean_gaps.detail: Paper: Δ-regular k-coloured multigraphs from the permutation model whose coloured local statistics converge to the iid-coloured regular tree (local-limit lemma, Friedman / Benjamini–Schramm), then a first-moment bound for rare matched walks. Lean: Cayley quotients of free groups crossed with *all* colourings (`GraphProducer.sequenceGraph`, `allColoringsGraph`), and an exact colouring count `GraphProducer.exists_rare_component` (GraphSequence.lean:17) for the bad-vertex fraction 20·V·|bad| < |X|. The edge test and averaging do not depend on this choice: they are stated for an arbitrary `PortGraph`.

lean_gaps.gap: The paper's Remark abstract-obstruction (tests.tex:143-174) is not a standalone Lean theorem.
lean_gaps.detail: Its generic content is spread over `PortGraph`-generic lemmas (`matched_exceptional_endpoint`, `exceptional_endpoint`, `edge_test`, `opposing_pairing_lower`, `signed_incidence_obstruction`). The assembly `finite_support_impossible` is specialised to `BlockConstruction.Block p`. Packaging the remark as a reusable theorem over abstract (N, A, G_m, h) data would cost roughly 60–120 lines. That would make design-reuse tests cleaner.
'F(M) is separable and not approximable' (Kalton 2012 Problem 1, via Kalton's Thm 4.4) is not in the Lean or the comparators (family.md).

In `BlockStatement` (DiscreteLipschitzFree.lean). Infinitude is proved separately (`BlockConstruction.infinite_block`) and is also forced by the obstruction, since F of a finite space is finite-dimensional and has 1-BAP.

As in the paper: `exceptionSet` puts every state into E_e when x is not `Good` (ScalarTests.lean:59). The Lean compatibility threshold `K+2L+1` (`Compatible`) matches the paper's strict bound '< 1+K+2L' up to the ≤/< convention.

comparator_chain_branches: Graph supply: `finite_support_impossible` → `GraphProducer.exists_rare_component` (GraphSequence.lean:17). This is the deterministic all-colourings count that replaces the paper's local-limit lemma.
The novelty pass gave dominator shares 0.37–0.39 for the obstruction subtree.

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph
lean_source.text:
structure PortGraph (X D : Type*) where
  reverse : D → D
  reverse_involutive : Function.Involutive reverse
  move : X → D → X
  move_reverse : ∀ x e, move (move x e) (reverse e) = x

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph.Matched
lean_source.text:
def Matched : X → S → List D → Prop
  | x, j, [] => compatible x j
  | x, j, e::w => compatible x j ∧ ∃ k, trans j k ∧ Matched (G.move x e) k w

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph.Good
lean_source.text:
def Good (n : ℕ) (x : X) : Prop :=
  ∀ j w, w.length = n → G.Reduced w → ¬ G.Matched compatible trans x j w

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph.RecordLength
OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph.record
lean_source.text:
def record (n : ℕ) (x : X) (e : D) (j : S) : ℕ :=
  Nat.findGreatest (G.RecordLength compatible trans x e j) n

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.Exceptional
lean_source.text:
def Exceptional (r : D → S → ℕ) (e : D) (j : S) : Prop :=
  ∀ g : D, g ≠ e → r g j < r e j

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.exceptional_unique
lean_source.text:
theorem exceptional_unique {r : D → S → ℕ} {e f : D} {j : S}
    (he : Exceptional r e j) (hf : Exceptional r f j) : e = f

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.PortGraph.matched_exceptional_endpoint
lean_source.text:
theorem matched_exceptional_endpoint {n : ℕ} {x : X} {e : D} {j k : S}
    (hx : G.Good compatible trans n x) (hy : G.Good compatible trans n (G.move x e))
    (hc : compatible x j) (hd : compatible (G.move x e) k)
    (ht : trans j k) (ht' : trans k j) :
    Exceptional (G.record compatible trans n x) e j ∨
      Exceptional (G.record compatible trans n (G.move x e)) (G.reverse e) k

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.MetricBlock.Compatible
lean_source.text:
def Compatible (x : X) (j : Point G color cap R) : Prop :=
  dist (originalLabel G color cap x) (label G color cap R j) ≤ (K+2*L+1 : ℕ)

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.MetricBlock.Transition
lean_source.text: def Transition (j k : Point G color cap R) : Prop := dist j k ≤ (2*L : ℕ)

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.MetricBlock.exceptionSet
OAI.DiscreteFree.MetricBlock.exceptional_endpoint
lean_source.text:
theorem exceptional_endpoint (S : Finset (Point G color cap R)) (n : ℕ) (x : X) (e : E)
    (j k : S) (hj : Compatible G color cap R L K x j.val)
    (hk : Compatible G color cap R L K (G.move x e) k.val)
    (ht : Transition G color cap R L j.val k.val) :
    j ∈ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n x e ∨
      k ∈ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n (G.move x e) (G.reverse e)

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.labelBump
lean_source.text:
def labelBump (h : M → N) (a : N) (L K : ℝ) (t : M) : ℝ :=
  L * max (1 - dist a (h t) / K) 0

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.opposing_scalar_extension
lean_source.text:
theorem opposing_scalar_extension (P Q : Set N) (b c : N → ℝ) (L : ℝ)
    (hL : 0 ≤ L) (hbLip : LipschitzWith 1 b) (hcLip : LipschitzWith 1 c)
    (hb : ∀ j, 0 ≤ b j ∧ b j ≤ L) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j ∧ c j ≤ L)
    (hcross : ∀ j ∈ P, ∀ k ∈ Q, dist j k < 2 * L → b j = 0 ∧ c k = 0) :
    ∃ f : N → ℝ, LipschitzWith 1 f ∧ (∀ z, |f z| ≤ L) ∧
      Set.EqOn f b P ∧ Set.EqOn f (fun z => -c z) Q

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.MetricBlock.edge_test
lean_source.text:
theorem edge_test (hL : 0 < L) (hK : 0 < K) (hLK : L ≤ K)
    (S : Finset (Point G color cap R)) (n : ℕ) (x : X) (e : E) :
    ∃ f : Point G color cap R → ℝ, LipschitzWith 1 f ∧ (∀ z, |f z| ≤ L) ∧
      (∀ j : S, j ∉ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n x e →
        f j.val = labelBump (label G color cap R) (originalLabel G color cap x) L K j.val) ∧
      (∀ j : S, j ∉ exceptionSet G color cap R L K S n (G.move x e) (G.reverse e) →
        f j.val = -labelBump (label G color cap R) (originalLabel G color cap (G.move x e)) L K j.val)

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.opposing_pairing_lower
lean_source.text:
theorem opposing_pairing_lower (μ ν f b c : S → ℝ) (E F : Set S) (L : ℝ)
    (hf : ∀ j, |f j| ≤ L)
    (hb : ∀ j, 0 ≤ b j ∧ b j ≤ L) (hc : ∀ j, 0 ≤ c j ∧ c j ≤ L)
    (he : ∀ j, j ∉ E → f j = b j)
    (hF : ∀ j, j ∉ F → f j = -c j) :
    pairing μ b + pairing ν c - 2 * L * (variationOn μ E + variationOn ν F) ≤
      pairing μ f - pairing ν f

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.signed_incidence_obstruction
lean_source.text:
theorem signed_incidence_obstruction [Nonempty X] [Nonempty D]
    (μ : X → S → ℝ) (E : X → D → Set S) (bad : Finset X)
    (rev : (X × D) ≃ (X × D)) (p V : ℝ)
    (hp : 0 < p) (hV : 0 ≤ V)
    (hTV : ∀ x, totalVariation (μ x) ≤ V)
    (hgood : ∀ x, x ∉ bad → ∀ j e f, j ∈ E x e → j ∈ E x f → e = f)
    (hdegree : 20 * V < (Fintype.card D : ℝ))
    (hbad : 20 * V * (bad.card : ℝ) < (Fintype.card X : ℝ))
    (hedge : ∀ e : X × D,
      3 * (10 * p) / 2 - 2 * (10 * p) *
        (variationOn (μ e.1) (E e.1 e.2) +
         variationOn (μ (rev e).1) (E (rev e).1 (rev e).2)) ≤ 2 * p) : False

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.GraphProducer.exists_rare_component
lean_source.text:
theorem exists_rare_component (Q H V : ℕ) (hQpos : 0 < Q) (hHpos : 0 < H)
    (hDpos : 0 < Nat.card (A × Bool))
    (hk : 2 * Nat.card (A × Bool) * Q * H < Nat.card C)
    (compatible : Vertex A C → S → Prop) (trans : S → S → Prop) (P : S → Finset C)
    (hP : ∀ j, (P j).card ≤ H)
    (hcolor : ∀ z j, compatible z j → sequenceColor A C z ∈ P j)
    (hQ : ∀ j, Fintype.card {k : S // trans j k} ≤ Q) :
    ∃ n : ℕ, 2 ≤ n ∧
      20 * V * Nat.card {z : (Cayley A n → C) × Cayley A n //
        ¬ (sequenceGraph A C).Good compatible trans n (intoSequence A C n z)} <
      Nat.card ((Cayley A n → C) × Cayley A n)

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.BlockConstruction.finite_support_impossible
lean_source.text:
theorem finite_support_impossible (hp : 1 ≤ p) (S : Finset (Block p)) (ho : base p ∈ S)
    (T : FreeSpace (base p) →L[ℝ] FreeSpace (base p))
    (hn : ‖T‖ ≤ 2*(p : ℝ))
    (hfixed : ∀ u, supportProjection (base p) (separation p) S (T u) = T u)
    (he : ∀ a ∈ anchors p, ‖T (delta (base p) a) - delta (base p) a‖ < 1) : False

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.BlockConstruction.obstruction
lean_source.text:
theorem obstruction (hp : 1 ≤ p)
    (T : FreeSpace (base p) →L[ℝ] FreeSpace (base p))
    (hfin : Module.Finite ℝ (LinearMap.range T.toLinearMap)) (hn : ‖T‖ ≤ (p : ℝ)) :
    ∃ a ∈ anchors p, (1/2 : ℝ) ≤ ‖T (delta (base p) a) - delta (base p) a‖

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.not_hasBAP_of_finite_obstruction
lean_source.text:
theorem not_hasBAP_of_finite_obstruction {M : Type*} [MetricSpace M] (o : M)
    (A : Finset M) (p ε : ℝ) (hε : 0 < ε)
    (hobs : ∀ T : FreeSpace o →L[ℝ] FreeSpace o,
      Module.Finite ℝ (LinearMap.range T.toLinearMap) → ‖T‖ ≤ p →
        ∃ a ∈ A, ε ≤ ‖T (delta o a) - delta o a‖)
    (Λ : ℝ) (hΛ : Λ ≤ p) : ¬ HasBAP (FreeSpace o) Λ

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.BlockStatement (comparator)
lean_source.text:
def BlockStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, 1 ≤ p → ∃ (M : Type) (d : MetricSpace M) (o : M),
    letI := d
    Countable M ∧ (∀ x y : M, x ≠ y → 1 ≤ dist x y) ∧
      (∀ x y : M, dist x y ≤ blockBound p) ∧
      ∃ A : Finset M, o ∈ A ∧ ∀ T : FreeSpace o →L[ℝ] FreeSpace o,
        Module.Finite ℝ (LinearMap.range T.toLinearMap) → ‖T‖ ≤ (p : ℝ) →
          ∃ a ∈ A, (1 / 2 : ℝ) ≤ ‖T (delta o a) - delta o a‖

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.MainStatement (comparator)
lean_source.text:
def MainStatement : Prop :=
  ∃ (M : Type) (d : MetricSpace M) (o : M),
    letI := d
    Countable M ∧ (∀ x y : M, x ≠ y → 1 ≤ dist x y) ∧
      (¬ Bornology.IsBounded (Set.univ : Set M)) ∧
      (¬ ProperSpace M) ∧ HasAP (FreeSpace o) ∧
      ∀ Λ : ℝ, 1 ≤ Λ → ¬ HasBAP (FreeSpace o) Λ

lean_source.name: OAI.DiscreteFree.RealL1RenormingStatement (comparator)
lean_source.text:
def RealL1RenormingStatement : Prop :=
  ∀ p : ℕ, 1 ≤ p → ∃ N : AddGroupNorm RealL1,
    (∀ (r : ℝ) (c : RealL1), N (r • c) = |r| * N c) ∧
    (∀ c : RealL1, (1 / 2 : ℝ) * ‖c‖ ≤ N c ∧ N c ≤ blockBound p * ‖c‖) ∧
    (let m : Module ℝ RealL1 := inferInstance
     letI : NormedAddCommGroup RealL1 := N.toNormedAddCommGroup
     ∃ s : NormedSpace ℝ RealL1, s.toModule = m ∧
       letI := s
       CompleteSpace RealL1 ∧
       HasBAP RealL1 (2 * blockBound p) ∧ ¬ HasBAP RealL1 (p : ℝ) ∧
         (p = 1 → ¬ HasBAP RealL1 1))

speedup_targets.title: Thm blocks via the paper's own random-graph route (design reuse of the abstract obstruction)
speedup_targets.statement: For each p ≥ 1 there is a bounded, 1-separated, countably infinite pointed metric space with a finite anchor set A such that every finite-rank T on F(M) with ‖T‖ ≤ p moves some δ_a by ≥ 1/2, where the graphs are random permutation-model Δ-regular graphs with iid colours (paper's Lemma local-limit + rare-walks), not Cayley quotients.
speedup_targets.reference: 330 preprint, blocks.tex, walks.tex:50-110, tests.tex Remark abstract-obstruction.
speedup_targets.status: known (the paper's own proof route; unrefereed)
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: Paper: about 4 pages for walks + local limit. Lean: the deterministic route `GraphProducer`/`ColorCounting`/`GraphSequence` is about 300 lines. The item part (`ScalarTests` + `SignedTests` + `GraphWalks`) is about 570 lines.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: `edge_test`, `exceptional_endpoint`, `matched_exceptional_endpoint`, `opposing_pairing_lower` and `signed_incidence_obstruction` are generic in the `PortGraph`, so only the bad-fraction bound has to be re-proved for the new graph family. This measures how portable the device is. Caveat: it is the same theorem by a sibling route, not a different theorem.

speedup_targets.title: Free spaces over diamond / Laakso graphs are not uniformly isomorphic to ℓ1ⁿ; projection constants of Lip0 over these graphs grow
speedup_targets.statement: d_BM(F(D_n), ℓ1^{N_n}) → ∞ for diamond graphs D_n, and the relative projection constants of Lip0(Laakso graphs) are unbounded.
speedup_targets.reference: Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii, Canad. J. Math. 72(3) (2020) 774–804, arXiv 1807.03814, https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.03814; Positivity 25 (2021), arXiv 2007.07949 [subagent-verified bibliographic data].
speedup_targets.current_proof_size: about 30 pp (CJM) + about 15 pp (Positivity). No formalization.
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Same shape of argument: one operator-norm bound, then averaging over a symmetric family. DKO average over cycle-preserving bijections (Grünbaum–Rudin), while 330 averages per-edge opposing tests over oriented incidences. An edge-test-style lower bound could replace the symmetrisation where the graphs lack a large automorphism group. Diamonds are not locally tree-like, though, so the records lemma has nothing to bite on. The analogy is loose.

speedup_targets.title: Lower estimates for the L1-distortion of transportation-cost spaces (planar grids, diamonds)
speedup_targets.statement: The transportation-cost (free) space over the m×m planar grid has L1-distortion Ω(log m); similar sharp bounds hold for diamond graphs and for {1..m}^d uniformly in d.
speedup_targets.reference: Gartland–Ostrovskii, 'Lower estimates for L1-distortion of transportation cost spaces', arXiv 2602.14852 (STOC 2026), https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.14852; Gartland–Ostrovskii–Rabani–Young, arXiv 2602.19434, https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.19434 [both subagent-verified].
speedup_targets.how_item_helps: Structurally the closest known method: systems of transportation problems on oriented edges (e⁺, e⁻) with ±1 sign matrices, averaged to force distortion for any linear map into ℓ1^m. The 330 edge test is also a signed per-oriented-edge test averaged over incidences, but adapted to the operator via discard sets. If the device helps anywhere outside BAP, this is the most plausible place. But planar grids are not locally tree-like and have no large degree to dilute over, so the records + degree-dilution part probably does not transfer.

open_problems.title: Kalton's question for proper / bounded-geometry uniformly discrete spaces
open_problems.statement: Does F(M) have the BAP for every uniformly discrete M that is proper (closed balls finite), e.g. every locally finite graph of bounded degree, or every finitely generated group with a word metric?
open_problems.reference: Kalton, Collect. Math. 55 (2004) 171–217, p. 185 (general question); Godefroy survey, Comment. Math. 55(2) (2015) 89–118, Problem 6.2, https://bibliotekanauki.pl/articles/746348.pdf; Hájek–Medina, arXiv 2112.03095, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.03095 (reduction to nets; Schauder bases for nets in some spaces) [subagent-verified]. I found no explicit listing of the proper/bounded-geometry special case.
open_problems.status: not found as a listed problem. 330 answers the general question with a non-proper space (the Lean proves `¬ ProperSpace M`), so the proper case becomes the natural residual question [status unverified].
open_problems.match: Operator-adapted edge tests on locally tree-like coloured graphs of large degree; the records lemma; degree dilution.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Direct transfer fails. The anchors attach infinitely many vertices at distance R, so each block is bounded but not proper. In a proper space a bounded block is finite, and then F is finite-dimensional with 1-BAP. Adaptation: replace one anchor per label by a finite hub tree of depth ~log, and let blocks be unbounded but uniformly locally finite. The averaging is already independent of |S|, but `bump_mass` uses d(x, a(x)) ≤ R with a fixed finite anchor set, so the 3L/4 bump bound breaks once anchors move to distance ~log|G|. This is a genuine obstacle. If it can be overcome, the payoff is large.

To be checked against the exact HM statement. Recorded here because it is open and may fall immediately.

open_problems.statement: If a separable Banach space admits λ-Lipschitz maps with relatively compact range converging to the identity uniformly on compacts, must it have the BAP?
open_problems.reference: Godefroy survey, Comment. Math. 55(2) (2015), Problem 6.3, https://bibliotekanauki.pl/articles/746348.pdf; Godefroy, CMUC 61 (2020) 187–193 may address it [subagent: not verified].

open_problems.match: The obstruction is linear (finite-rank operators of norm ≤ p against anchors). 330's F(M) fails BAP and, via Kalton 2012, is also not approximable, so it does not answer 6.3.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Adaptation: a nonlinear edge test. For a Lipschitz map Φ: F(M) → F(M) with relatively compact range, compose with the per-edge 1-Lipschitz tests f_e. The measure representation μ_x (affine weights) is linear-specific, so one would need a barycentric replacement. Unclear.

open_problems.title: Does every Banach space with the BAP admit an equivalent norm with the MAP?
open_problems.statement: Casazza's handbook problem (as cited by Godefroy–Ozawa, Problems 3.8/3.12): BAP ⇒ MAP after renorming?
open_problems.reference: Casazza, 'Approximation properties', Handbook of the Geometry of Banach Spaces Vol. 1 (2001) [problem numbers via Godefroy–Ozawa 2014; wording unverified]; Godefroy–Lancien–Zizler, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 44 (2014), arXiv 1207.2958, Problem 18 [subagent-verified].
open_problems.match: 330's RealL1Renorming produces norms on ℓ1 failing MAP, i.e. the opposite direction (ℓ1 already has MAP in its usual norm).
open_problems.how_item_helps: Mostly not. A counterexample needs an obstruction invariant under all renormings, but the anchor obstruction is p-quantitative and degrades by the renorming constant. Recorded as a direction where the device is expected not to help.

open_problems.title: Godefroy survey Problem 6.4: is the MAP (or a dimension-free BAP constant) available for F(M), M ⊂ ℝⁿ?
open_problems.statement: For M ⊂ ℝⁿ, does F(M) have the MAP? Known: λ-BAP with λ ≤ C√n (Lancien–Pernecká). Is a bound independent of n possible?
open_problems.reference: Godefroy survey (2015), Problem 6.4; Lancien–Pernecká, J. Funct. Anal. 264 (2013) [memory]; still called open in Hájek–Medina 2021 [subagent].
open_problems.match: Opposite regime. The device needs exponentially growing locally tree-like structure at bounded scale, which doubling subsets of ℝⁿ cannot host. A lower bound λ_n → ∞ would need families in growing dimension.
open_problems.how_item_helps: Probably not. Embedding the 330 blocks into ℝⁿ costs distortion that grows with the block size, and a bounded infinite 1-separated set cannot sit in ℝⁿ at all. Listed so the experiment can confirm the device's limits.

negative_controls.setting: Doubling (e.g. Euclidean) uniformly discrete spaces, and nets in finite-dimensional spaces
negative_controls.why: F(M) has the BAP for doubling M (Lancien–Pernecká 2013 [memory]), and nets in ℝⁿ even give Schauder bases (Hájek–Pernecká; Hájek–Medina [subagent]). The device needs large-degree locally tree-like graphs at bounded scale (degree Δ > 20V with V = 1+4pB). Doubling spaces cannot host them, so any claimed obstruction there signals a bug.

negative_controls.setting: Renormings of ℓ_p (1 < p < ∞) and of c0
negative_controls.why: Every equivalent norm on these spaces has MAP: AP is an isomorphism invariant, and a space with AP that is reflexive, or whose dual is separable with AP, has MAP (Grothendieck; standard, e.g. Casazza's handbook chapter [memory]). So the RealL1Renorming pattern cannot transfer from ℓ1 to these spaces.

negative_controls.setting: Drop the operator-norm bound, or raise it to ≥ 2B_p on a single block
negative_controls.why: The same space has AP (`MainConstruction.hasAP`), and each bounded block has 2B_p-BAP (`bounded_separated_hasBAP`, used in Renorming.lean). So the edge-test contradiction (2p > 11p, which uses ‖T‖ ≤ 2p) cannot extend to unbounded or ≥ 2B_p-norm finite-rank operators. Good for checking that a prover does not over-apply `signed_incidence_obstruction`.

precedent_check.summary: The records / exceptional-direction lemma (I31) is a close variant of Ben-David–Childs–Gilyén–Kretschmer–Podder–Wang (arXiv 2006.12760, Lemma 58; checked in the novelty pass). This caps the sub-lemma at N2 but does not cover the operator-adapted opposing tests with discard sets or the incidence averaging. The structurally nearest 2026 work is Gartland–Ostrovskii (arXiv 2602.14852, STOC 2026): signed systems of transportation problems on oriented edges, averaged, to lower-bound L1-distortion. It is fixed (not operator-adapted), has no discard sets, and lives on grids and diamonds, so it is not an earlier equivalent. Its relation to I32/I33 deserves an expert look. Smith (arXiv 2509.00722) is a prior result, not a prior device: complete discrete, not uniformly discrete, via descriptive set theory. No Sept–Oct 2026 paper citing 330 or using an edge-test argument was found, but arXiv keyword search does not catch citations and the web quota cut the search short.
items: Ben-David et al. 2020, Lemma 58: close variant of the records lemma (N2), already in L.
Gartland–Ostrovskii 2026: closest technique in Banach/metric geometry. Signed oriented-edge tests, but not operator-adapted. Not an equivalent; flag for expert check.
Dilworth–Kutzarova–Ostrovskii 2020: 'average over symmetries, then one operator norm bound'. Generic pattern, not equivalent.
Smith 2025: prior partial answer to Kalton by a different method.
